subject: SOC 2 acceptance: which file satisfies procurement?
messages:
From: Sam Reed <sam.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify acceptable SOC 2 package for Acme procurement

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

Quick one from procurement: our security team pulled the SOC 2 files Redwood uploaded and flagged that the Type II PDF on your portal is for the period ending 2023-12-31. They say that's outside our rolling 12-month window. We also received a one-page "interim bridge" (Draft_Signed_Bridge_2026.pdf) that appears to cover the gap, but they aren't sure if the bridge + older Type II will be accepted or if you need a fully reissued 2026 Type II.

Can you confirm what Acme should upload to satisfy the procurement checklist? Options on our side are: (A) Accept your 2023 Type II + a signed bridge from the auditor; (B) require the newly reissued 2026 Type II once available; or (C) need both the bridge and the in-progress auditor contact and timeline. We have a vendor approval gate next Friday and would like to finalize documents this week if possible.

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_2023.pdf (from your portal), Draft_Signed_Bridge_2026.pdf (uploaded by your security team)

Thanks,
Sam Reed
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Health

---
Note: Procurement wants an explicit acceptance statement they can store in their vendor file.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reed <sam.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 10:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify acceptable SOC 2 package for Acme procurement

Sam — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: option (A) can be acceptable in many procurement workflows but with specific conditions.

High level requirements we ask for when relying on an older Type II plus a bridge:
- The bridge must be signed by the same independent auditor who issued the Type II (auditor name and signature block visible).
- The bridge must explicitly state the audit coverage gap dates and that there were no control exceptions in the interim (or list any exceptions).
- The Type II report + bridge together must cover a continuous audit period that includes the last 12 months or a reasonable bridge explaining coverage.
- We need the auditor firm and contact (email/phone) for procurement verification.

If the bridge is informal or unsigned we can't accept it; if you expect the reissued Type II before your vendor approval gate, option (B) is also fine. If you go with (A) we'll need the signed bridge and the auditor contact by EOD Thursday to meet your Friday gate.

Marissa / Olga — looping you for compliance/legal confirmation but my operational ask is: Sam, please have your security/procurement upload the signed bridge PDF and confirm the auditor firm. If possible, include a short cover email from the auditor to speed acceptance.

Jordan Blake
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: redwood_soc2_checklist.xlsx (checklist we typically provide to customers)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reed <sam.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 15:36:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify acceptable SOC 2 package for Acme procurement

Hi Sam — thanks. A few compliance points to make acceptance unambiguous on your side: 

Checklist (what Acme needs to provide to move to "accepted" status):
1) Final PDF of the last issued SOC 2 Type II report (we have 2023 on file) — include report metadata (audit period start/end, report ID if present).
2) Signed bridge letter from the auditor that explicitly:
   - Names the auditor firm and partner signing the bridge,
   - States the period the bridge covers and confirms whether any exceptions were noted,
   - Is dated and signed.
3) If the bridge references any compensating controls or remediation, include the remediation timelines/evidence (can be a short spreadsheet).
4) Auditor contact information (email/phone) so Acme/your team can confirm authenticity; procurement often calls the auditor.

If you can provide items 1–4 we will provide Acme a concise "acceptance statement" that you can drop in your vendor file (this is what procurement is asking for). If the new Type II will be issued before your approval window and it's a true Type II covering at least a 12-month period that overlaps current date, that also closes the gap — in that case we just need the final PDF.

Also, if Acme is being asked for SIG/CAIQ answers as well, upload an export (.xlsx or .csv) and we'll do a cursory mapping; sometimes procurement insists on both SOC 2 + SIG. We can help validate mapping but won't act as the final authority — procurement will still need to record acceptance.

One operational note: signed bridges are often PDF-scanned with a partner signature page. Please avoid unsigned draft language. If the bridge is issued as a "management representation" from your auditor without signature, that will not satisfy our procurement team.

Happy to jump on a short call if helpful — Jordan, Olga, if you have any nuance to add.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0143

From: Sam Reed <sam.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify acceptable SOC 2 package for Acme procurement

Thanks — that's exactly the level of detail our procurement team wanted. We'll request the signed bridge (signed by RSM LLP, partner listed, with explicit gap dates) and ask the auditor to include a short cover email with contact details.

Action items on our side: upload signed bridge + auditor email to your Drive link by Thursday EOD; if RSM can reissue the full Type II before Friday we'll prefer that, but plan (A) looks like our working path.

I'll confirm once the files are in the folder and request your acceptance statement for our vendor file. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sam
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Health
